A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LAION-C research work. All 32 pages, including Appendix A.1–A.8, figures, tables and equations, are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, a fine-tuning experiment and a psychophysical study with 19 analyzed participants and 11,400 trials, with results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark evaluations, fine-tuning results and human-study outcomes, including the detailed appendix results.

M1.justification: The six distortion-generation procedures, benchmark construction and superclass prediction aggregation remain unchanged in Section 2 and Appendix A.4. No algorithmic component or inference procedure is added or revised.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ImageNet-derived, 16-class LAION-C coverage with six distortion types, the same comparison benchmarks and the same human and model evaluation scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across the corresponding evaluations. Tables 10–11 retain the same vision models, GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5 Pro and human comparisons.

E3.justification: Both versions retain five distortion intensities, 273 source images per superclass, the same human-study timing and sample sizes, VLM subsampling, metrics and fine-tuning design. No experimental setting is revised.

E4.justification: The fine-tuning solvability analysis, human–model error-consistency analysis, occlusion measurements and VLM case studies are unchanged, including Tables 8–9 and Figures 8–13.

E5.justification: The 95% confidence-interval reporting in Figures 6 and 11 and the sample-size justification remain unchanged. Neither version adds or revises seed information, repeated-run counts or statistical testing procedures.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 10 reports the same LAION-C accuracies for GPT-4o (54.1%), Gemini 1.5 Pro (50.2%) and the best human observer (55.2%); the fine-tuning results also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The covariate-shift formulation in Section 2.1 and Cohen’s kappa definition in Appendix A.3 are unchanged. No mathematical assumption, derivation, theorem or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims: LAION-C challenges web-scale vision models with novel distortions, and the best models match or outperform human observers. Their scope and strength do not change.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning different human and model strategies, possible background shortcuts and architectural advantages are retained. Section 4 preserves the same unresolved mechanisms, performance-limit questions and warning against training on the OOD benchmark.

D1.justification: Augmentation parameters, laboratory hardware and software, model identifiers, VLM prompts, preprocessing instructions and code/data access information are unchanged. The added funding acknowledgement supplies no new technical or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work discussion in Appendix A.1 are unchanged, as is the positioning relative to earlier robustness benchmarks and human–machine comparisons. No cited work is added or removed.

P1.justification: v2 changes three appendix references from 'Appx.' to 'Sec.', updates the arXiv version/date stamp and adds acknowledgement of BMFTR grant 01IS24085C (OPENHAFM). The scientific prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Edited references cause limited text rewrapping on page 5, and the expanded acknowledgement reflows on page 9. Figures 1–13 and Tables 1–11 retain their content, design, numbering and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly expands funding attribution and makes small reference and typesetting edits. The scientific evidence, reasoning, limitations and reproducibility information remain unchanged across the main text and appendices, leaving no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
